message_short: BCG caliber must match barrel caliber
message_long: Your BCG is spec'd for a different caliber than your barrel. These parts will not function together. A 5.56 NATO barrel is compatible with both 5.56 NATO and .223 Wylde BCGs. .300 BLK requires a dedicated .300 BLK BCG.

message_short: Magazine caliber must match barrel caliber
message_long: Your magazine is loaded for a different caliber than your barrel. This is a potentially dangerous mismatch. Always ensure your magazine caliber matches your barrel caliber.

message_short: Muzzle device thread pitch must match barrel thread
message_long: The thread pitch on your muzzle device does not match your barrel's muzzle threads. 5.56/.223 barrels typically use 1/2x28 threads; .308/.300 BLK barrels use 5/8x24 threads.

message_short: Gas block bore must match barrel journal diameter
message_long: Your gas block's bore diameter does not match your barrel's gas block journal. Common sizes are 0.625", 0.750", 0.875", and 0.936". These parts cannot be installed together.

message_short: Gas tube length must match barrel gas system
message_long: Your gas tube length does not match the gas system on your barrel. Pistol-length gas systems require a pistol gas tube (~4"), carbine requires carbine (~7"), mid-length requires mid-length (~9.75"), and rifle requires a rifle-length gas tube (~12").

message_short: Handguard must be shorter than barrel
message_long: Your handguard is longer than or equal to your barrel length. The handguard must be shorter than the barrel to allow for the gas block and proper installation.

message_short: Gas block profile incompatible with handguard clearance
message_long: Your handguard requires a low-profile gas block but your selected gas block has a standard/F-height profile. A standard gas block will not fit inside this handguard.

message_short: Stock tube spec must match buffer tube spec
message_long: Your stock is designed for a different buffer tube specification than your selected buffer tube. Mil-spec stocks require a mil-spec tube (1.148" OD), commercial stocks require a commercial tube (1.168" OD).

message_short: Brace tube spec must match buffer tube spec
message_long: Your pistol brace requires a different buffer tube specification. Verify the brace's tube compatibility (mil-spec, commercial, or pistol tube) matches your buffer tube.

message_short: Trigger pin diameter must match lower receiver
message_long: Your trigger's pin diameter does not match your lower receiver. Standard mil-spec lowers use 0.154" pins. Some lowers (like CMMG) use 0.170" pins. Mismatched pins will not function.

message_short: Hammer pin diameter must match lower receiver
message_long: Your hammer's pin diameter does not match your lower receiver. Standard mil-spec lowers use 0.154" pins. Some lowers use 0.170" pins. Mismatched pins will not install.

message_short: Stock and pistol brace cannot both be selected
message_long: A stock and a pistol brace are mutually exclusive. You can have one or the other, not both. A stock converts the firearm to a rifle configuration; a brace keeps it in pistol configuration.

message_short: Foregrip mount type must match handguard rail system
message_long: Your foregrip's mount type (M-LOK, KeyMod, or Picatinny) does not match your handguard's accessory rail system. These cannot be attached together.

message_short: Light/laser mount type must match handguard rail system
message_long: Your light or laser's mount type does not match your handguard's accessory rail system. M-LOK accessories require M-LOK slots; Picatinny accessories require a Picatinny rail section.

message_short: Bipod mount type must match handguard rail system
message_long: Your bipod's mount type does not match your handguard's accessory rail system. An adapter may be needed.

message_short: Buffer weight may be suboptimal for this gas system
message_long: Your buffer weight may not be ideally matched to your barrel's gas system. Pistol/carbine gas systems typically run best with lighter carbine buffers (3oz). Rifle-length gas systems benefit from heavier H2/H3 buffers. This may cause reliability issues — particularly over-cycling.

message_short: Handguard length very close to barrel — installation may be difficult
message_long: Your handguard is within 1" of your barrel length. While technically compatible, this can make installation difficult and may leave very little clearance around the muzzle area.

message_short: Suppressor use — consider heavier buffer (H2/H3)
message_long: Suppressors increase backpressure significantly, causing over-cycling. Consider upgrading to a heavier H2 (4.6oz) or H3 (5.4oz) buffer, and ideally an adjustable gas block, to maintain reliable operation with a suppressor.

message_short: Oversized charging handle latch may conflict with low-mounted optics
message_long: Your charging handle has an oversized latch. When used with a large, low-mounted optic, the latch may contact the objective bell or mount. Verify clearance before finalizing your optic setup.

message_short: ⚠️ SBR Configuration Detected
message_long: This configuration meets the ATF definition of a Short Barreled Rifle (SBR) — a rifle with a barrel under 16" in length. SBRs are NFA (National Firearms Act) items regulated under 26 USC § 5845. Manufacturing or possessing an SBR without prior ATF approval and payment of the $200 tax stamp (Form 1 or Form 4) is a federal felony. This tool does not provide legal advice. Consult a qualified firearms attorney before building.

message_short: ⚠️ Pistol Brace Configuration — Rules in Flux
message_long: This configuration uses a barrel under 16" with a pistol brace. Pistol brace regulations have been subject to ongoing ATF rulemaking and federal court challenges. The legal status of pistol braces has changed multiple times. Verify current ATF rules and applicable state law before building or possessing this configuration. This tool does not provide legal advice.

message_short: ⚠️ NFA Suppressor Detected
message_long: Your build includes a suppressor (silencer). Suppressors are regulated as NFA items under 26 USC § 5845(a)(7). Manufacturing or possessing a suppressor requires prior ATF approval via Form 1 (make) or Form 4 (transfer), plus a $200 tax stamp. Suppressors are prohibited in some states. This tool does not provide legal advice. Consult a qualified firearms attorney and verify your state's laws before purchasing or building a suppressor.

message_short: ℹ️ BCG gas key may not be staked
message_long: Your BCG's gas key should be properly staked to the carrier for long-term reliability. An unstaked gas key can back out under fire, causing malfunctions. Verify staking before use.

message_short: ℹ️ Twist rate note for bullet weight selection
message_long: Barrel twist rate affects optimal bullet weight. 1:7 twist stabilizes heavier 62-77gr projectiles. 1:8 twist is versatile across 55-77gr. 1:9 twist is best for lighter 55-62gr bullets. Match your ammunition to your barrel's twist rate for best accuracy.
